name: Single-Agent Doxorubicin for Soft Tissue Sarcoma
histology: soft tissue sarcoma (histology-agnostic anthracycline backbone across the common adult subtypes)

biomarkers.note: Single-agent doxorubicin is a cytotoxic anthracycline backbone for soft tissue sarcoma and is not biomarker-restricted. Histology (rather than a molecular biomarker) guides subtype-specific alternatives. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Soft Tissue Sarcoma v5.2026, Systemic Therapy Agents and Regimens with Activity in Soft Tissue Sarcoma Subtypes.

lineOfTherapy: first-line systemic option (single-agent or as the backbone of doxorubicin-based combinations) for advanced, metastatic, or unresectable soft tissue sarcoma, and used in the neoadjuvant/adjuvant setting for high-risk resectable disease

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: advanced, metastatic, or unresectable soft tissue sarcoma of a doxorubicin-responsive histology
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v5.2026, Systemic Therapy Agents and Regimens (Doxorubicin, SARC-F)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate baseline cardiac function (LVEF) before anthracycline exposure

drugs.name: DOXOrubicin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 175842 (GeDDiS trial: six cycles of single-agent doxorubicin at 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 175842. DOXOrubicin 75 mg/m2 IV on day 1 every 21 days (GeDDiS trial single-agent doxorubicin arm, the standard first-line comparator in advanced soft tissue sarcoma). Anthracycline cumulative lifetime cap: warn 450, hard 550 mg/m2 (conventional anthracycline ceiling, not a value from the source subtype table). ISMP tall-man applied (DOXOrubicin). Track cumulative dose; obtain baseline and periodic LVEF. Doxorubicin-based COMBINATIONS (for example AIM, doxorubicin plus ifosfamide/mesna) and the histology-directed alternative gemcitabine plus docetaxel are listed by the guideline; see supportiveCare/notes for the sourced gemcitabine/docetaxel dosing.

regimen.cycles: six cycles were used in the referenced GeDDiS trial; continue per response and the cumulative anthracycline ceiling, physician determined

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 is highly-to-moderately emetogenic (regimen-dependent); give prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier on the day of treatment

supportiveCare: antiemetics: doxorubicin single-agent at 60 to 75 mg/m2 is on the moderate-to-high emetic-risk boundary; prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.
cardiac surveillance: baseline LVEF and cumulative anthracycline dose tracking (warn 450, hard 550 mg/m2).
G-CSF: assess febrile-neutropenia risk; add primary prophylaxis for higher-risk patients or dose-dense doxorubicin-based combinations.

SOURCED ALTERNATIVE (gemcitabine plus docetaxel): gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 IV over 90 minutes on days 1 and 8 plus docetaxel 100 mg/m2 IV on day 8 with G-CSF, every 21 days (DeVita 12th ed., line 176028, Hensley regimen, Table 50.6); a fully-sourced histology-directed alternative (for example for leiomyosarcoma) modeled here as a note, not as a separate combination in this single-agent protocol.

monitoring: cardiac function (LVEF) at baseline and as clinically indicated

doseModificationRules.condition: cumulative doxorubicin approaching 450 mg/m2 (warn) or 550 mg/m2 (hard)
doseModificationRules.text: Warn at 450 mg/m2 and stop at the 550 mg/m2 hard cap; reassess cardiac function; physician decides on continuation.

doseModificationRules.condition: decline in LVEF or clinical cardiotoxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and obtain cardiology review before further anthracycline.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: line 175842 (GeDDiS: single-agent doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks); line 176028 (gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 days 1 and 8 + docetaxel 100 mg/m2 day 8 with G-CSF q21d, Hensley, Table 50.6)

guideline.locator: Systemic Therapy Agents and Regimens with Activity in Soft Tissue Sarcoma Subtypes (Doxorubicin single-agent and doxorubicin-based combinations such as AIM; gemcitabine/docetaxel as a histology-directed option), SARC-F

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for single-agent doxorubicin in soft tissue sarcoma (StewardMD reference disease soft_tissue_sarcoma; histology-agnostic anthracycline backbone). The dose (DOXOrubicin 75 mg/m2 IV every 21 days) is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. line 175842 (GeDDiS trial single-agent doxorubicin arm, the standard first-line comparator in advanced soft tissue sarcoma). Regimen identity is cross-referenced to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Soft Tissue Sarcoma v5.2026, Systemic Therapy Agents and Regimens (SARC-F), which lists doxorubicin and doxorubicin-based combinations but does not print the milligram dose. The anthracycline cumulative lifetime cap (warn 450, hard 550 mg/m2) is the conventional anthracycline ceiling, not a value from the subtype table. A fully-sourced histology-directed alternative (gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 days 1 and 8 plus docetaxel 100 mg/m2 day 8 with G-CSF, q21d; DeVita 12th ed. line 176028, Hensley) is documented as a note rather than modeled as a separate combination in this single-agent protocol. ISMP tall-man applied (DOXOrubicin). No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
